summary: Create an invented workshop around readable power transmission, crafted pressure vessels and layered repair while keeping historical and engineering claims out of decorative machinery.
objective: A viewer can identify the driver, follow one motion chain to a useful output, inspect how a vessel or machine is assembled, and distinguish hot, moving and safe interaction zones.
intent_signals: set the scene in a steampunk workshop
build a brass machine room with linked motion
create an inspectable fantastical steam engine
example_prompts: Design a fictional steampunk repair workshop where one handwheel drives a readable shaft-and-linkage chain, with an inspectable vessel and clearly separate decorative steam.
negative_signals: brass material applied to every object
decorative steam presented as computed pressure flow
not_for: Historical claims about actual steam technology, labor, dress or architecture without separate primary research.
Engineering or safety analysis of pressure vessels, gearing, boilers or rotating equipment.
A thermodynamic or fluid simulation unless its variables, equations, units and validation are separately declared.

principles: Give the workshop a legible job and one dominant power chain: input, transmission, supported shafts or linkages, and an output that visibly changes state.
Craft machines as assemblies with shells, seams, fasteners, bearings, pipe supports, access clearances and repair evidence. Ornament should follow structure rather than replace it.
Use brass, copper, iron, timber, leather, glass and textile as distinct authored surface roles; variation in roughness, oxidation, soot and polished touch zones should explain use.
Separate warm practical light around occupied work from cooler window or skylight fill, preserving silhouettes around spokes, rods and pipes and readable contrast at controls.
Prefer constrained or authored kinematics for a deterministic fictional machine. Add rigid-body contact, pressure or thermal physics only when the task asks a question that those models answer.
implementation: Arrange a driver station, transmission bay, workbench and output machine around clear walking and maintenance space. Route pipes and shafts through brackets, glands and bearings instead of through unrelated solids.
Build a hero vessel from body courses, end caps, necks, flanges, valves, gauge mount and feet or saddles. Make inspection seams and service access readable; do not imply code compliance.

Assign dark iron to frames and high-load visual masses, copper or brass to selected fittings and warm highlights, timber or leather to hand-contact areas, and glass to protected gauges or sight features.

Derive linked angular motion from one driver parameter and declared tooth counts or linkage phase where ratios matter. A stopped driver stops downstream parts unless a clutch, flywheel or stored-state behavior is explicitly authored.

Treat steam puffs, gauge tremor and lamp flutter as labeled decorative or state-driven effects. If a gauge indicates a variable, the pointer and machine state share one authority rather than playing unrelated loops.
Use an overview to reveal the whole motion chain and an inspection view for the vessel, bearing or valve; provide pause, single-step where useful and reset.
observable_checks: From the overview, identify the input, follow every transmission connection and state what output the machine drives; unsupported or decorative gears are visually distinct.
Rotate or step the driver through a cycle: connected shafts, meshing gears and linkages preserve their declared ratios and phase without tooth sliding or sudden reversal.
Inspect the hero vessel or machine: supports, seams, access points, valve/gauge mounts and pipe attachments remain legible under close light.
Compare powered, stopped and reset states: the gauge, output, lamps and state-driven vapor agree with the same fictional state and return exactly.
Turn decorative vapor off: the mechanism and its motion chain remain understandable, showing that particles are atmosphere rather than the simulation authority.
Read controls against both warm and cool backgrounds; focus, selection and hazard cues retain shape or label distinctions in addition to color.

known_limits: Authored fictional theme guidance; no rendered artifact, historical-authenticity review, mechanism test or runtime improvement has been observed for this record.
Visible gears, gauges, pipes and vapor do not establish feasible power, pressure, temperature, efficiency or safe operation.
Surface terms describe visual material roles; they do not supply measured metal, wood, leather, glass or textile properties.
creative_affordances: Scale the workshop from a watchmaker's bench to an airship hangar while preserving one traceable job and power chain.
Combine with whimsical, ornate, soot-heavy, polished salon or improvised repair directions; keep material roles and control contrast deliberate.
Use a non-steam fictional driver such as a hand crank, spring store or fantastical source when the story benefits, and label its behavior as invented.
